answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn reputation or claim rewards. A registry binds each lock to one identity, while slashing burns the stake if linked accounts are caught laundering rewards. The thread of a long-running voyage then carries reputation across verified work, not fresh names; a fable about unlimited identities fails when every extra persona ties up real capital and risks forfeiture. The cost rises with each sybil, even if detection is imperfect.
